candidate_relations.reason: Both are extra-axial spinal masses causing cord compression, but meningioma is a solid neoplasm with different MRI characteristics (typically iso-to-hypointense T1, variable T2, homogeneous enhancement), whereas the described rim enhancement with no internal enhancement and low T2 signal favor a hemorrhagic synovial cyst; these are incompatible diagnostic entities despite overlapping anatomical location
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Spinal meningioma is an extra-axial posterolateral mass that can cause cord compression at C7-T1, but the MRI signal characteristics (homogeneously low T2 signal, rim enhancement without internal enhancement) are more consistent with a hemorrhagic cystic lesion than a meningioma, which typically shows homogeneous enhancement; the reference diagnosis specifies a hemorrhagic synovial cyst, a distinct entity

case_quality_flags: MRI signal pattern (low T2, rim-only enhancement) is atypical for meningioma and strongly favors hemorrhagic cystic lesion; absence of facet joint pathology description limits synovial cyst confirmation but reference diagnosis is hemorrhagic synovial cyst
